messages.content: You are a computer science tutor. Answer clearly and accurately in at most 150 words.
Explain why a queue is useful for handling incoming print jobs. Give one concrete example and one limitation.

runs.output_text:
A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without losing requests.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if User A submits a 50-page report and User B submits a 1-page memo, the queue ensures User A’s job starts first. The printer processes pages in the exact order received, maintaining predictable workflow and preventing smaller jobs from indefinitely blocking larger ones.

**Limitation:** Standard queues lack priority handling. A critical, urgent document cannot jump ahead of a long, low-priority job already in line. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive tasks, requiring more complex priority queues or scheduling algorithms to resolve.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without losing requests.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if Alice, Bob, and Charlie send documents at 9:00 AM, 9:01 AM, and 9:02 AM respectively, the queue ensures Alice’s job prints first, followed by Bob’s, then Charlie’s, regardless of when the printer actually starts processing.

**Limitation:** A standard queue lacks priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after hundreds of large, low-priority files, it must wait until all preceding jobs finish. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive tasks, requiring a priority queue instead.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing starvation. Printers are single-resource devices; without a queue, concurrent requests would cause race conditions or require complex locking mechanisms. The queue decouples the submission of jobs from their execution, allowing the system to buffer requests while the printer processes them sequentially.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, ten employees send documents to a shared printer simultaneously. The queue stores these jobs in the order received. The printer pulls the first job, prints it, then pulls the second, ensuring no user’s document is skipped or printed out of turn.

**Limitation:** A standard queue lacks priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after a large batch of low-priority files, it must wait until all preceding jobs finish. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive tasks unless a priority queue is implemented instead.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) order, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without losing requests.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if User A submits a 50-page report and User B submits a 1-page memo, the queue ensures User A’s job starts first. The printer processes pages sequentially, preventing User B’s small job from interrupting or corrupting the larger print stream.

**Limitation:** A standard queue lacks priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after a long queue of low-priority jobs, it must wait until all preceding jobs finish. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive tasks, requiring a priority queue instead.
